top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on one simple, general mechanism: at the magic wavelength the light shifts of the two clock levels cancel, so thousands of atoms can be held free of Doppler and recoil shifts. It has a clear origin in Katori's proposal and first strontium demonstration, a decisive realisation by Ye's group at the 10^-18 level, and independent reproduction and cross-comparison in several national laboratories, with real physics outputs (relativistic geodesy, bounds on drifting constants and dark matter). The two-laureate allocation is uncontested and the citation scope is tight. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a strong, well-understood theory-plus-experiment story but has a single supporter and a more contested credit and scope question, and it follows the recent topological prizes; no award is the weakest option when a mature, reproduced achievement with a clean allocation exists.
